text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Iranian Cultural Centre in Lahore was set ablaze on Sunday by activists of sectarian militant organisation, Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan.
- The army was deployed in Jhang after the killing of SSP chief Zia-ur-Rahman Faruqi in a Lahore bomb blast that claimed 26 lives.
- Though sugar imported by the government from India has arrived, it remains a rare commodity in the market.
- The light rain after a dry spell of two months will have a positive impact on the wheat crop in rain-fed areas, farmers said.
- Arrival of unpressed cotton from fields to ginneries has started showing a declining trend and a shortfall of about 0.5 million 375-lb bales has been noticed till January 15.
- The caretaker government on Sunday restored the operation of cellular phones in Karachi and other parts of Sindh.
- Procedural impediments and lack of proper export finance schemes are hampering the export growth of Pakistan.
- Pakistan will examine the acceleration of private sector investment in airline and airport infrastructure at a meeting on Tuesday.
- Businessmen in Lahore observed a strike after Saturday's tragic bomb blast.
- The cost of production of textiles will increase two percent after increases in the prices of gas and furnace oil.
- The government has decided to arrest leaders of all sectarian groups and put the paramilitary Rangers on alert to control law and order.
- The police have arrested a man who later confessed to setting off the device at the Sessions Court building in Lahore that killed 26 people on Saturday.
